title: TradeYa
shortOutcome: A live skill-trade marketplace being hardened from a broad web product into a maintainable foundation for mobile expansion.
role: Product designer, full-stack developer, and operator
ownership: I own the product direction, interface, application architecture, Firebase integration, quality systems, deployment workflow, and current maintainability work. Firebase, React, and the other platform dependencies remain third-party technology.

evidence.label: Production
evidence.detail: The marketplace is operating on its public custom domain while the current facelift and reliability pass continue.
evidence.provenance: Public production route and repository deployment configuration

evidence.label: Marketplace scope
evidence.detail: The product covers skill trades, collaborations, challenges, profiles, messaging, reviews, and community activity.
evidence.provenance: Repository AGENTS.md and feature-domain source structure

evidence.label: Quality gates
evidence.detail: The repository defines TypeScript, lint, Jest, Playwright, Firebase security, asset-bloat, and production build checks.
evidence.provenance: Repository package.json scripts and AGENTS.md verification contract
evidence.limitation: The active hardening phase means individual features still require current verification before release claims.

problem.title: Creative collaboration breaks when trust, scope, and exchange live in separate places.
body: People can offer useful skills and still struggle to find a fair counterpart, define the exchange, communicate through delivery, and preserve evidence of the result.
TradeYa puts discovery, trade proposals, collaboration, messaging, reviews, and community participation into one product while keeping the exchange centered on skills rather than cash.

ownership.title: A first-party product spanning interface, marketplace state, and production operations.
body: I direct and implement the product, including the React application, Firebase data paths, marketplace workflows, design system, tests, security checks, and deployment operations.
The current work is not a claim that every feature is finished. The facelift is paired with feature verification and maintainability work before mobile expansion.

systemMap.label: Member identity
systemMap.detail: Authentication, profiles, skills, reputation, and availability establish who can participate.

systemMap.label: Marketplace discovery
systemMap.detail: Trades, collaborations, challenges, builders, and community activity expose possible matches.

systemMap.label: Proposal state
systemMap.detail: Scope, participants, status, and evidence move through explicit marketplace records.

systemMap.label: Trust controls
systemMap.detail: Validation, Firestore rules, reviews, and moderation boundaries constrain unsafe transitions.

systemMap.label: Collaboration loop
systemMap.detail: Messaging, notifications, progress, and delivery evidence support the work after a match.

systemMap.label: Verification and repair
systemMap.detail: Tests, production checks, and the current hardening pass return broken or inconsistent flows to implementation.

decisions.title: Treat Firestore shape as a product contract
decisions.decision: Keep denormalized display fields, indexes, security rules, and migration behavior explicit rather than letting UI needs mutate data ad hoc.
decisions.consequence: Marketplace surfaces can evolve without silently weakening trust or breaking older records.

decisions.title: Harden the web product before mobile expansion
decisions.decision: Finish the facelift alongside feature verification and maintainability work before treating iOS as an active product surface.
decisions.consequence: Mobile work can start from understood behavior instead of duplicating unresolved web debt.

decisions.title: Use real marketplace content as the visual proof
decisions.decision: Prefer real trades, collaborations, challenges, builders, and activity over abstract dashboard statistics.
decisions.consequence: The interface communicates user value instead of decorating incomplete product state.

buildRecord.label: 01 / MODEL
buildRecord.title: Marketplace domains
buildRecord.detail: Trades, collaborations, challenges, profiles, messages, reviews, and evidence have explicit service and data boundaries.

buildRecord.label: 02 / BUILD
buildRecord.title: React product system
buildRecord.detail: TypeScript, Vite, React Query, shared UI primitives, and feature modules form the client application.

buildRecord.label: 03 / OPERATE
buildRecord.title: Firebase production layer
buildRecord.detail: Authentication, Firestore, Cloud Functions, storage, indexes, security rules, and migration tooling support production state.

buildRecord.label: 04 / VERIFY
buildRecord.title: Layered quality gates
buildRecord.detail: Type checking, lint, unit tests, browser tests, security checks, asset budgets, and builds cover different failure classes.

failures.title: Feature breadth created maintenance debt
failures.observed: A large marketplace surface accumulated duplicate scripts, dependency age, and inconsistent implementation paths.
failures.response: The active phase pairs the facelift with explicit feature checks, shared primitives, dependency review, and maintainability gates.

failures.title: Visual polish could outrun functional proof
failures.observed: A facelift can make an unfinished flow look complete before its data and interaction paths are verified.
failures.response: Treat browser verification and feature behavior as release gates instead of accepting appearance alone.

failures.title: Mobile parity was easy to describe too early
failures.observed: The roadmap names iOS and Android outcomes while the web foundation still requires stabilization.
failures.response: Label mobile as preparation and sequence it after web behavior and maintainability are verified.

currentStatus.title: Live, under active hardening, and preparing for mobile expansion.
body: TradeYa is live while the current phase refreshes the interface, checks feature behavior, and reduces maintenance risk. iOS development is the next platform direction, not a shipped capability.
